reasons: The verse asks whether gold (சொர்னம்) grows when mercury and sulphur (சூதம், கெந்தி) are heated in a crucible by those ignorant of the art, implying it does not; the finding that mercury becomes gold only by nuclear reaction, never chemical processing, is direct evidence for that, though it also rules out the 'right' alchemy the verse leaves open.

The verse asks whether gold (சொர்னம்) will grow when mercury and sulphur (சூதம், கெந்தி) are put in the crucible (புடம்), implying it will not; the finding that mercury becomes gold only by nuclear reactions, never chemical processing, is direct evidence for that hypothesis. The verse leaves open that true வாதம் might succeed, which the finding would contradict.

The verse states a testable rule: a day is twenty-one thousand six hundred சுவாசம், days shorten as breaths go (போனதனால் நாள்குறைந்து), and if they do not go there is no dying; the finding says a fixed breath stock rests only on cross-species correlation and slowing breath has not been shown to extend human life.

The verse states a life of a hundred years is 21,600 breaths a day (இருபத்தோராயிரத்தோடறுநூறு சுவாசம்), that days shorten as breaths go out, and that if they do not go out there is no going (போகாவிட்டால் போவதில்லை); the finding that the fixed-stock idea rests only on a cross-species correlation and that slowing breath has not been shown to extend life tells against that hypothesis.

The verse claims the five letters சிவாய call back by their means (உபாயம்இட்டு அழைக்குமே) the breath (வாயுவை) that went out the doorless gate; the finding that mantra recitation slows breathing to about six a minute supports a claim that reciting a mantra governs the breath, though the verse may instead mean restoring life after death.

The verse claims the five-syllable mantra (சிவாயஅஞ் செழுத்து) calls back the breath (வாயுவை அழைக்குமே); the finding that mantra recitation slows breathing to about six a minute is evidence that recitation does act on the breath, though the doorless gate (கபாடமற்ற வாசல்) is a cipher left aside.

The verse claims the root fire's heat is kindled by the breath (மூலஅங்கி தணல் எழுப்பி வாயுவால்); the finding that tummo and breathing practice can raise body temperature bears on a breath-generated heat, though the root fire and nectar are yogic terms.

The verse says the yogi kindles the heat of the root fire with the breath (மூலஅங்கி தணல்எழுப்பி வாயுவால்); the finding that trained breath and tummo practitioners can raise body temperature bears on a claim that breath practice generates inner heat, though the 'root fire' is a yogic notion rather than measured temperature.

The verse claims that striking again and again (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து) with the sword of the அஞ்செழுத்து cuts down the dense forest of the mind (மனக்காட்டை); the finding that silent repetition of a word reduces cortical and default-mode activity bears on this, but it is labelled speculative so the direction stays neither.

The verse asks to cut down the dense forest of the mind (அடர்ந்த மனக்காட்டை) by striking again and again (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து) with the five-letter mantra; the finding that repeating a single word reduces widespread cortical activity bears on the idea that repetition quiets the mind, but it is speculative and does not settle the verse's claim.

The verse decodes its own cipher (இடைகலையே சந்த்ர காந்தம், பின்கலை ஆதித்தன்) and claims that drawing breath up the left channel and holding it in the sushumna (இடைகலையி லேற வாங்கிச் சுழுமுனையில் கும்பித்து) entrances you; the finding that one-nostril effects rest on small inconsistent studies bears on this but points neither way.

The verse prescribes drawing the breath up the left channel and holding it (இடைகலையி லேற வாங்கிச் சுழுமுனையில் கும்பித்து), claiming this brings trance (சொக்கு வீரே); the finding bears on whether one-sided breathing has specific effects, but the evidence is inconsistent and reading இடைகலை as the left nostril is a gloss.

The stanza boasts that the furnace-work will make gold (பொன்னை யாக்குவோம், with கருமான் உலை, the forge); the finding says gold can be made only by nuclear reactions, never by chemical or alchemical processing, which counts against a literal reading, though the verse may mean inner work.

The verse boasts of working the forge (கருமா னுலையிலே தீயை மூட்டுவோம்) and making gold (பொன்னை யாக்குவோம்), an alchemical transmutation claim; the finding that gold comes from mercury only by nuclear reactions, never by chemical or furnace processing, is evidence against it, though the lines may be partly figurative.

The verse says boasts of fixed flying mercury (கவனசூதமுடிந்ததென்பார்) and a magnet made into a cup are the trickery (புரட்டு) of world-alchemy (புவனவாதை) by which alchemists make a living; the finding that mercury cannot be chemically turned into gold supports the verse's charge that outward alchemy is fraud, though the boasts it names are not transmutation as such.

The verse calls alchemists' boasts of fixed flying mercury (கவனசூதம்) and wonder-works a trick to make a living (புரட்டாலே பிழைக்கிறார்); the finding that mercury cannot be transmuted by chemical or alchemical means supports this scepticism about mercury alchemy.

The verse says those who promise alchemical silver and gold (வாதம்செய்வேன், பொன்) take the money and run, i.e. the promise is a fraud; the finding that gold cannot be made by alchemical processing supports the falsity of the promise, though the verse itself is about the trick, not chemistry.

The verse depicts those who promise alchemical silver and gold (வாதம்செய்வேன் வெள்ளியும் ... தங்கமும்) as cheats who take the fee and flee; the finding that gold cannot be made by chemical or alchemical processing supports the verse's treatment of such promises as fraud, though the verse does not itself state transmutation impossible.

The verse calls the tale of joining lead with gold (வங்கமுக்தங்கஞ் சேர்த்திருக்கதை) a disgrace while alchemists melt லிங்கம்; the finding that gold cannot be made chemically supports the debunking, though the cinnabar sense of லிங்கம் is a technical gloss.

The verse calls the tale of joining lead with gold (வங்கம் ... தங்கம் சேர்த்திருக்கதை) a disgrace (பங்கம்), i.e. a fraud; the finding that chemical processing cannot make gold supports that judgement, though the verse's claim is moral rather than chemical.

The verse boasts செம்பொன் னாக்குவோம், that the Siddhars will turn the three worlds into red gold; the finding that gold can be made only by nuclear reactions, never by alchemical processing, is evidence against such a transmutation claim, though the boast is cosmic hyperbole rather than a stated procedure.

The verse boasts that the Siddhars will turn the three worlds into red gold (செம்பொன் னாக்குவோம்); the finding that gold can be made from mercury only by nuclear reactions, never by alchemy, tells against the alchemical power claimed, though the boast is cosmic hyperbole rather than a stated procedure.

The verse claims no caste mark is stamped on flesh, skin or bone (இறைச்சிதோல் எலும்பினும் இலக்கமிட்டு இருக்குதோ); the finding of shared mixed ancestry with endogamy arising only a few thousand years ago bears on this, but cuts both ways since endogamy did leave population-level genetic structure.

The verse asks whether caste is marked on flesh, skin or bone (இறைச்சிதோல் எலும்பினும் இலக்கமிட்டு இருக்குதோ), denying a bodily basis for caste; the finding of shared mixed ancestry and late onset of endogamy bears on this and largely supports it, though endogamy since then has left group-level genetic differences.

The verse claims that by உப்பு (salt, likely the alchemical muppu) the body is hardened for கற்பாந்தங் கோடி, crores of aeons, before மூப்பு (old age) sets in; the finding that no hallmark of ageing has yet been reversed in humans is evidence against this claim of an ageless body.

The verse claims that by the salt (உப்பதனால்) the body hardens and lasts for crores of aeons (கற்பாந்தங் கோடி காய மிதுவலுத்து) before old age (மூப்பு) turns it to calx; the finding that no hallmark of ageing has yet been reversed in humans tells against such a claim, though what the salt is is left in cipher and the syntax is broken.

The verse argues against caste from the body: senses, womb-birth and needs are the same for all (ஐம்புலன்கள் ... ஒக்குமோ, யோனியில் பிறந்து, உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே). The finding that Indian groups share mixed ancestry and that strict endogamy is comparatively recent bears on the claim that birth-group divisions have no deep natural basis, though endogamy has since left genetic structure.

The verse argues against caste from the body: the same senses (ஐம்புலன்கள்), the same birth from the womb (யோனியில் பிறந்து), the same food, sleep and pleasure for you and me (உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே); the finding that Indian groups share mixed ancestry and that strict endogamy is relatively recent bears on and broadly supports the claim that caste is not a difference of kind, though the verse does not speak of descent.

The verse names a calcination of பாஷாணம் in a crucible (குகை, புடம்) and asks what is in it, dismissing the alchemical product; the finding of heavy-metal poisoning from Siddha and Ayurvedic preparations bears on the worth of such products and is consistent with the dismissal, though it concerns mostly lead and mercury.

The verse dismisses furnace-processed arsenic (பாஷாணம்) with 'what is there in it' (இருப்பதென்னடி), denying the value of the preparation; the finding of heavy-metal poisonings linked to Siddha and Ayurvedic preparations bears on that scepticism and supports it.

The verse claims plainly that the body will not perish (உடல் மாயாதல்லவோ) through an inner practice; the finding that no hallmark of ageing has yet been reversed in humans is evidence against such an undying body, though the practice itself (காசாம் வேர், வாயாறு) needs a cipher gloss and is not tested.

The verse claims a practice makes the body not perish (உடல் மாயாதல்லவோ); the ageing-hallmarks finding, that no hallmark of ageing has been reversed in humans, is evidence against a deathless body, though the practice itself is in cipher (காசாம்வேரு, வாயாற்று).

The verse claims that in nishtai the 'he' and 'I' fall away (தான் நான் என அற்று) while the body persists; the speculative finding that self-loss in deep meditation is reported in distinct forms bears on the first claim without settling it.

The verse reports a state in nishtai where 'he' and 'I' are gone (தான் நான் என அற்று) and the self is known by itself; the finding describes such self-loss states in very experienced meditators, but it is speculative and descriptive, so it does not point either way.
